tasks.instructions: Experiment E1 (tests H48): sc_kernel: owner-converted resident weights, sync 1 gates only d (seven sc rows). STEP 0, price the chain (<= 5 B200 min). Read the parent card's sc_kernel phase-A order and smem plan in parts. Build two timing-only stubs of sc_kernel; wrong results are allowed and neither is ever shipped. (a) Skip the weight pass and leave the fp16 scratch as garbage; everything else unchanged. (b) As (a), and also skip the post-sync TMA of A, so GEMM1 reads an A image already in smem. Run harness_time interleaved x3 against the parent at 1,192 / 2,96 / 4,192 / 1,160 / 8,192. Take globaltimer stamps of phase-A end and sync-1 release from the working warps. Gate: stub (a) saves >= 1.2 us mean over those rows. If not, stop, record the prices as findings and ship the parent unchanged. STEP 1, GEMM1 weights. At entry each GEMM1 CTA issues cp.async.bulk of its own fp32 W1 rows (128 hidden x C, 98 KB at C=192), beside the plane copies. After its conv units it converts them into its resident SW128 K-major fp16 A image, using the validated address function. In the same pass it computes u_k (rowsum of the rounded fp16(lnw*W1) values) and v_k = W1.lnb + b1. Issue every load before any shuffle, fully unrolled (lesson j). STEP 2, GEMM2 weights. GEMM2 owners bulk-copy their fp32 W2 slice right after sync 1, or at entry if smem allows, and convert it during GEMM1 or the sync-2 wait. b2' = W2.gb + b2 comes from per-K-slice partial sums of the owners; the output reduction is already additive. Reuse raw fp32 landing areas as unit buffers after conversion. If 4,192 / 8,192 exceed 227 KB, convert in two halves through one staging area, or keep the scratch path on those shapes (shape-only dispatch). Keep cg grid.sync on sc_kernel: the flat barrier lost 1-2 us there in r9. STEP 3, checks. cuobjdump -res-usage must show STACK 0 on every sc instantiation. run_tests 16/16 with portal-order re-runs. The u_k summation order changes, so log precision afresh over 10 seeded rounds (seed 200, fp64 reference, harness generators) on all seven sc rows: max |err| and count beyond own atol. The sc class sits at 79-89 % of atol, and any beyond-atol element blocks shipping (fallback: hi/lo split per H22). STEP 4: harness_time interleaved x3 against r11-merge-b on the seven sc rows; record per-row deltas and merge picks. Success: -1.5 us rented or better on at least 5 of the 7 sc rows vs r11-merge-b interleaved x3, 0 beyond-atol elements over 10 rounds, STACK 0 Refuted if: stub (a) saves < 1.2 us mean (the weight chain is already overlapped), or the built version gains < 0.7 us on 4 or more of the 7 rows This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. You may discard the parent's design entirely; it is given for reference. Test the idea's core assumption with probe_b200 first (seconds per probe). If the idea does not pan out, still return your best version of it as the candidate and record what you learned in the card's findings: negative results are valuable and go into the lab notebook for later rounds. CUDA C++ uses the two-file layout. Set the card's tests: field to the hypothesis id(s). OPERATOR NOTE (rules): every red.add / atomic / bulk-reduce target is zeroed or prefilled inside this call before its first add (the workspace is torch.empty, uninitialised); grid, cluster or per-image counters (and departure counters) live in a module-level __device__ buffer self-reset by the last arriver, never in the workspace; spins are plain ld.acquire loops. No PDL; stamps compiled out of the shipped build; target_hardware [B200] only; TMA descriptors encoded every call; no state kept between calls (no converted weights, no cached outputs) except shape-keyed attributes set to one maximal value and a per-shape cuBLASLt heuristic; cache hints only on our own workspace buffers; timing-only stubs that skip work must never be the shipped candidate; cuobjdump -res-usage STACK 0 on the shipped build.

Experiment E2 (tests H49): tc_kernel: GRN scale in the GEMM1 epilogue behind per-image counters, no g, single-accumulator GEMM2. STEP 0 (<= 5 B200 min). Read the parent card in parts to see which tc paths r11-merge-b runs per row: the 7x7 C=768 MP=2 path, the r10 tc2 path on 16,384, and the pair path at B >= 16. Stamp the parent with globaltimer from the working warps; check STACK on the stamp build too. Rows: 32,768 / 16,768 / 8,768 / 16,384. Stamp the GEMM1 per-tile mainloop and the post-accumulator split (pass 1, g pass, stores), the GEMM2 phase and ns per stage, and clk per MMA instruction in the mainloops. Compare the clk with r11 K's straight-line table (N=64 50, N=128 66, N=224 114 clk). If D issues at >= 90 clk per instruction at N <= 128, precomputed descriptors with an unrolled k16 loop may go into the build as a separately stamped change. If the parent card does not record the flat-barrier stress loop, run it now: 1500 calls at 8,768 and 16,384 against the torch reference. Any failure reverts tc_kernel to cg grid.sync. STEP 1, the 7x7 C=768 path. The GEMM1 epilogue keeps the GELU output h in fp32 registers (thread = hidden row, its share of the columns). It reduces the per-(image,k) sumsq inside the CTA and red.adds sum_k gf into a [B] buffer zeroed in phase A. It then release-arrives on a per-image counter, CUTLASS-style: bar.sync, then red.release.gpu from one thread. The expected count is the number of tiles touching image b. Order tiles image-major, and let a CTA wait only after its earlier tiles are done; in the co-resident cooperative grid the wait graph then has no cycle. Spin with ld.acquire, never __nanosleep. Counters self-reset through a departure counter. Then compute inv_b = 1/(mean_k gf + eps) and store h' = fp16(h * (1 + gw*gf*inv_b)) through the staged coalesced store. gb stays in b2'. While the epilogue warps wait, the MMA warp may already issue the CTA's next tile into a second TMEM accumulator. GEMM2 drops g and runs one accumulator over h' alone. Spend the freed stage bytes on more depth, or on MP=2 over h' only, or on 2x tokens per stage, and pick per row. STEP 2: carry the change to the 14x14 paths (on the tc2 path it replaces the in-smem B-scale), to the pair path, and to 2,768 / 8,768. STEP 3: STACK 0 on every instantiation (holding h in registers at N=208 risks spills; split columns over the 4 warps of a quadrant). run_tests 16/16 with portal-order re-runs. h' is new arithmetic, so log precision afresh over 10 rounds (fp64 reference) on every row shipped. Then run harness_time interleaved x3 against r11-merge-b on the six wide-C rows. Stamp the image wait (median and max per tile) and the GEMM2 phase. Success: >= 10 % rented on 32,768 and on 16,768 and >= 5 % on 8,768 vs r11-merge-b interleaved x3; image-wait median <= 1.5 us; 0 beyond-atol elements; STACK 0 Refuted if: < 4 % on both 32,768 and 16,768 after STEP 1, or image-wait median > 2.5 us (per-image skew eats the g saving), or the GEMM2 stage time does not fall without g (stages latency-bound rather than byte- or MMA-bound) This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. Experiment E3 (tests H43): Top rows STEP 2: tcgen05 GEMM1 + epilogue warps in the fixed-role pass-1 kernel, then the K0/K3/cuBLASLt tail. Resume from r10-i-e3-tmaconv-gate. i_tmaconv_gate.cu holds the validated 3-D TMA box ring: box {W+8, R+6, 16}, start {-4, h0-3, b*C+g*16}, OOB zero fill. STEP 2: one pass-1 kernel for 64,96, then the 32,128 instantiation. 512 threads, 1 CTA/SM, persistent over 224-token tiles. N >= 128 now runs at the MMA ideal in 1SM mode (r11 K), so smaller tiles are allowed where they balance better, e.g. the 32,128 tail. Roles are warp-uniform: (a) 1 TMA warp: x boxes plus a W1' A ring of 2 x 16 KB. (b) 8 conv warps: register-blocked patches from the gate, fp16 d written into the MN-major SW128 B tile with G's r9 address function, LN partials into smem. (c) 1 MMA warp: kind::f16, elect.sync issue, d released per 16-channel group (one k16 step of K=96), 2 x 224-column TMEM ping-pong. (d) Epilogue warps in a multiple of 4 (TMEM lane-quadrant rule): LN fold rs*(acc - mu*u) + v, A&S erfc GELU, per-(image,k) sumsq red.add into [B][4C], coalesced fp16 h stores through a per-warp smem transpose. Smem budget from the gate: x ring 123 KB + d 48 KB + LN 14 KB + A ring 32 KB. r11 K finding: MUFU-heavy epilogue warps cost the warps sharing their SMSP 30-40 %. The FMA pipe binds here, so check that the conv warps keep >= 85 % of their gate rate, and place the producer and MMA warps accordingly. Stamp conv / MMA / epilogue per tile. Validate h for tile 0 and the last tile against torch before timing. Gate: pass 1 <= 400 us rented at 64,96. STEP 3, only if the gate passes: build the tail from the notebook recipes. K0: W1' = fp16(lnw*W1) with u and v, fp16 W2, gsum zeroed. K3: per-image W2_b = fp16(s_b*W2), grid (B, C/16), one row per warp, __launch_bounds__(512,2). GEMM2: cuBLASLt batched swap-AB with beta 1 on C = x, b2' as hi/lo K-augmentation columns paired with constant rows written by pass 1, top-1 heuristic. run_tests 16/16 with portal-order re-runs; STACK 0; a 10-round fp64 precision log on 64,96 and 32,128. Then harness_time interleaved x3 against r11-merge-b on the two rows. If STEP 3 does not finish, archive the pass-1 kernel with its stamps behind the r0 anchor (as r10 did) and record what remains. Success: pass 1 <= 400 us rented at 64,96; with the tail, rows <= 650 us (64,96) and <= 190 us (32,128) rented vs about 857 / 228 for r11-merge-b in the same container, 0 beyond-atol elements Refuted if: pass 1 > 520 us at 64,96 after tuning (less than 22 % better than G's 668 us), or the role layout cannot fit the 128-register cap and 227 KB without dropping below 8 conv warps This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%. Experiment E4 (tests H50): New design: Toeplitz tensor-core depthwise conv gate for 64,96 and 32,128. New lineage, built from scratch around pool idea I15. STEP 0, no GPU. Run a numpy fp64 simulation at 64,96 and 32,128 (harness generators, 2 seeds) of the end-to-end output error when the conv uses (a) TF32-rounded (RNE) x and taps, or (b) fp16 hi/lo x with fp16 taps, optionally hi/lo taps. In both cases d is then rounded to fp16 and the rest follows the fp16 pipeline (fp16(lnw*W1), h16, fp16(s_b*W2)). Report max |err| as a share of each row's atol and pick the cheapest form that stays <= 75 %. STEP 1, single-plane probe on one (b,c) plane of 64,96. Out rows [h][w'] = sum_{i=0..6} X[h+i-3][:] @ T_i, where T_i[w,w'] = k_c[i, w-w'+3] is banded and built in smem per channel. Run it on tcgen05 with x landed by one 3-D TMA box: TFLOAT32 map for kind::tf32, OOB zero fill for the halo, inner start a multiple of 16 B (start at w=-4 and offset the taps). Solve the row shift i without 7 copies of x. Options: the smem descriptor's matrix base-offset field for starts not aligned to the 1024-B swizzle atom; an unswizzled K-major core-matrix layout; or the operand orientation that puts the shift on the side that tolerates it. Validate against torch conv2d to fp32-class error before timing anything. STEP 2, a standalone conv kernel for 64,96 and 32,128, persistent over (image, row band) work. Each CTA covers all C channels of its band, so the per-token LN sum and sumsq stay CTA-local. It writes d fp16 in a padded [c][token] layout (usable as the MN-major B operand of a later GEMM1) plus per-token mean and rstd. Use compile-time variants only for ablations. Report: time after the flush, clk per MMA against the r11 K STEP 0a table, the tensor-pipe share, and STACK. Ship nothing to the merge: the archived solution is the r0 anchor with the probe source behind #if 0 (as r10 I did), and run_tests 16/16. Success: conv + d write + LN partials <= 100 us rented at 64,96 and <= 25 us at 32,128; d within 1-2 fp16 ulp of fp16(torch conv2d); simulated end-to-end max error <= 75 % of atol Refuted if: > 180 us at 64,96 (no clear edge over I's 233.8 us FMA conv), or the row shift cannot be expressed without 3x or more smem or L2 traffic, or every precision form exceeds 85 % of atol in the simulation This is an EXPLORATION task: the goal is to learn whether this idea can move some size band by 3% or more on the portal, not to edge out the current best by 0.1%.
